description: Three revenue bands holding 6, 6 and 4 orders. Write the conditions in the wrong order and one band collects twelve orders while another collects none, with no error anywhere.

title: DAX Time Intelligence: DATEADD, TOTALYTD and the Month That Is Not There
description: Without a date table the report skips April entirely and calls May a 6 percent drop on March. With one, DATEADD works, YTD reaches 9,890, and April shows as the minus 100 percent it was.

title: Standard Deviation in Everyday Words: What It Measures and How to Read It
description: Built by hand from sixteen orders: why the deviations sum to zero, why you square them, why the divisor is 15 and not 16, and what a standard deviation of 236.81 actually tells you.

title: Tableau Aliases: Rename What Readers See Without Touching the Data
description: An alias renames the members of a discrete dimension so a chart says East instead of E. Why measures, dates and continuous dimensions cannot have one, how aliases differ from renaming a field, and the published data source limit.

title: Tableau Desktop Foundations Exam: 40 Questions, and 20 Right Passes It
description: The exam facts from Salesforce's own guide: 40 scored questions plus up to five unscored, 70 minutes, 48% to pass, four domains weighted 23/37/25/15, testing on Tableau 2022.3. What that arithmetic says about where to study.

title: Tableau Dashboard Extensions: What They Add, and What They Can Read
description: An extension is a third-party web application running inside your dashboard. The two hosting kinds, what each permission level gives access to, how to add one, and the print behavior that catches people out.

title: Tableau Hierarchies: One Drag Puts a Drill-Down on Every Chart
description: Drop one field on another and Tableau builds a hierarchy, which puts plus and minus drill controls on every view that uses it. How to build one, why the order matters, and how a hierarchy differs from a group, a set and a bin.

title: Your Tableau Dashboard Needs Two or Three Views, Not Eight
description: Tableau's own guidance is to limit a dashboard to two or three views. How to pick which sheets survive, where the important one goes, and how to choose between fixed, automatic and range sizing.

title: Tableau Sorting: A Rule That Re-Runs, or an Order You Froze
description: The four Tableau sort options, and the one question that separates them: does this sort re-evaluate when new data arrives? Includes the alphabetic sort that puts Item 10 before Item 2, and how nested sorts behave when you drill.

title: Absolute vs Relative References in Excel: What the Dollar Sign Locks
description: What the dollar sign does in an Excel formula, and why a copied column can be wrong while its first row is right. The four F4 states in order, mixed references, and when you need no dollar sign at all.

title: Row-Level Security in Power BI: Who Gets Filtered and Who Does Not
description: RLS only restricts users with the Viewer role. Workspace Admins, Members and Contributors see every row, by design. Two roles is a union rather than an intersection. Worked on sixteen orders with the arithmetic printed.

title: SUM vs SUMX in DAX: Why a Row-by-Row Calculation Needs an Iterator
description: SUM takes one column. SUMX takes a table and an expression and evaluates it on every row before adding up. Worked on sixteen orders, with the 9,890 that reads 214,625 and the average that is wrong by 0.73 points.

title: Contribution Margin and Break-Even: The Fixed Cost That Does Not Belong in the Unit
description: Contribution margin is price minus variable cost, and only variable cost. Putting a share of the fixed cost inside the unit turns a 750-unit break-even into 12,000. The worked model, the SQL, and what a 10% discount really costs.

title: Gross vs Operating vs Net Margin: What Each One Tells You
description: Three margins from one income statement, each stripping out one more layer of cost. The SQL division that quietly returns 0, the averaged monthly margins that miss by 3.1 points, and how to read a margin against a benchmark.

title: Current Ratio vs Quick Ratio, and Debt to Equity
description: Three balance-sheet ratios and the definitions that decide their answers. A 2.40 current ratio that is $200,000 short of paying the bills, a quick ratio that is 1.04 or 1.10 on the same day, and debt to equity of 0.70 or 1.04 for one company.

title: Net Present Value (NPV): How to Discount Cash Flows and Read the Answer
description: NPV worked on a five-year project, one row at a time. The discount factor, why the same cash flows are worth +$137,236 at 10% and -$2,347 at 20%, and the SQL that returns 350,000 because the discounting never happened.

title: COMMENT ON TABLE: How to Store a Table Description in the Database Itself
description: COMMENT ON TABLE and COMMENT ON COLUMN store a description inside the database. The exact syntax in PostgreSQL and Oracle, the different syntax MySQL and SQL Server need, and how to read them back.

title: SQL Comment Syntax by Database: MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, SQLite, Oracle
description: The comment character for every major database, in one table, plus the four differences that break a query when it moves between engines.
